posts.caption: Photograph by @paulnicklen // After spending months of camping on the sea ice, I finally took off in my ultralight airplane with my friend and ace pilot, Brian Knutsen.  We expected to see a few Narwhals from the air but never did I expect to find a large group of male narwhal surrounded by the most stunning pattern and shape in the sea ice.  Once we saw this, we landed immediately and walked up within 4 feet of hundreds of narwhals.  Please #follow me on @paulnicklen to see my favorite images from this encounter.  There really are unicorns out there in the wild.  The spiral, ivory tusks just so happens to be on a beautiful and very real whale rather than a fictitious horse.  #unicornsofthesea #unicorn #narwhal #whale #nature #gratitude #naturelovers #beauty @natgeo @natgeocreative #climatechange #climatechangeisreal

Photo by @CarltonWard // Newly hatched Kemp's ridley turtles scramble toward the Gulf of Mexico at Padre Island National Seashore in Texas. The Kemp's ridley is the most endangered of the world's seven species of sea turtles. All sea turtles are threatened or endangered. Five species can be found in the Gulf, where coastal development has contributed to population declines. At Padre Island, which is part of the world's largest barrier island system, eggs from nests are gathered by National Park Service biologists and incubated in a nursery to help increase the number of hatchlings to start their lives in the waves. #gulfofmexico #seaturtle #NationalParks Please #followme @carltonward.

Photo by @bertiegregory // There's nothing quite like seeing a marine mammal underwater. Encountering bottlenose dolphins in the northern Red Sea is pretty common. More often than not however, they tease you with just a brief flyby. This female and calf though honoured me with their presence for over an hour! The calf stuck right alongside it's mother but from time to time, the mother would give permission to the calf to take a closer look. It would zip over to me and open its mouth letting out audible squeaks and clicks.

Photo by @andywcoleman // We found this South Maui beach during a morning run.  It was a beautiful, long crescent stretch of sand with only a couple of people playing with their dogs.  We decided to return for sunset and learned that this beach was no secret.  There was one wedding and three other couples with wedding photographers.  We were still able to find a spot photograph another great Maui sunset.  We had to use a map to see that the name of this area is Palauea Beach.  Palauea translates to "lazy" in ancient Hawaiian, which seems perfect for this quiet little spot.

Half the park is after dark. When most people are sleeping, the stars come out to play. I love astrophotography, not only because I get to see the stars at night but also because I mostly have them all to myself. The quiet, cold night air is intoxicating, as are the stars that glimmer above. The downside is waking up at ungodly hours and crawling out of the warm bed. But I cannot remember a time when I wasn't glad I forced myself up and out of bed, no matter how strong the urge to stay sleeping. Fighting inertia is something at which every photographer must be a master

Below soaring 1,500 foot cliffs, on one side lies Mexico and the other, the United States. This is the Río Grande River that flows through Santa Elena Canyon in Big Bend National Park and separates the two countries. You can hike for a few miles inside the canyon downstream for views like this. Or better yet, take a kayak for a two to three day trip through the canyon for even more dramatic views

Photo by @andywcoleman // Earlier this week, the government of Ecuador announced the creation of a more than 15,000-square-mile marine sanctuary around two of the northern Galápagos islands: Darwin and Wolf. Together with 21 smaller conservation areas scattered through the volcanic archipelago, over 18,000 square miles, or about one third of the water around the Galápagos Islands, are fully protected from fishing and other extractive industries.  With the convergence of four major currents in the area, the waters of the Galapagos is rich in nutrients and biodiversity.  We saw fantastic sea life here on a recent National Geographic Expedition, including this extraordinarily graceful spotted eagle ray.  #NatGeoExpeditions #PristineSeas

Photo by @KristaRossow // Every year at springtime, it seems like light pink clouds descend from the sky in the form of cherry trees and snuggle the edge of the Tidal Basin in Washington, DC. This shot from a few years back shows the Jefferson Memorial framed by blossoms illuminated by the setting sun. It is now almost cherry blossom peak bloom on the National Mall in DC and, if you find yourself there, I recommend to make the effort to arrive before sunrise or stay through sunset for the best light on the blossoms.

Tired of cold weather, after Cuyahoga Valley National Park we headed as far south as we could in search of warmer climates and vivid color. We found both (and an amazing national park) on the border of Mexico in southwest Texas in Big Bend National Park. This is one of the great sunrise hikes we did there: grapevine hills trail to the precariously perched balanced rock. The show stopper is the sight pictured here, a photogenic rock that has been balanced in this position for a millennia. However, the whole trail is full of huge rounded boulders that are also very photogenic and are so tempting to climb upon. Just watch out for snakes!

Photo by @TimLaman. Just published in the Apr/May 2016 NatGeo Traveler magazine, check out the story of how our family spends our summers.  With a mom (Cheryl Knott) who is an Orangutan researcher, and a dad (@TimLaman) who is a @NatGeo photographer, our kids @RussLaman and @JessicaLaman get dragged to the rain forests of Borneo every summer to their mom’s research site in #GunungPalung National Park, whether they like it or not. Photograph by @JohnStanmeyer "My thoughts and prayers to all in Brussels" ~ John Stanmeyer

Baryo, 50, from Ranupani Village near Bormo, praying to the main deity, Hyang Widi Wasa and the God of the Mountain during the Kasada Ceremonies on Mount Bromo, East Java.

I took this portrait while on the National Geographic assignment, a story I proposed to the magazine called, Volcano Gods. Living in Indonesia at the time, I began working on the mystical elements of how the Indonesian society spiritually interacts with volcanoes or what many consider are the navels, the bellybuttons of the earth.

My first time to Mount Bromo was in 1999, ironically also at a sacred Kasada ceremony. On this return years later, I was here for the spirituality that swirls around this gobsmacking volcano once every year under a full moon. Baryo, a Hindu priest and shaman, was deep in trance while incense veiled him on a very cold evening at 7,650 ft (2,329 meters) above sea level, creating an aura that naturally befit an utterly unique religious ceremony.

This photograph ran in the January 2008 issue of the magazine, pleased it made it to the final edit as a poetic means to illustrate what is truly one of the more fascinating and beautiful cultures on earth — Indonesia.

All my best, John Stanmeyer

Photo @chrisburkard // In the mid 20th century these purple flowers, known as Alaskan Lupine, were introduced to Iceland in order to help prevent erosion and spur reforestation. The volcanic soil makes it difficult for other forms of plants to grow, but this particular flower thrives in it. In some ways it has taken over the landscapes When it’s not blanketed in snow, the flowers accent the epic sunsets perfectly. It's a good reason to always have your camera close by while driving.

Photo by @andywcoleman // Camouflage can be a key to survival in the wild. These cheetah cubs are too young to hunt with their mother, so she needs to stash them somewhere safe while she searches for food. Another safari vehicle saw her hide these five cubs in some thick brush in the morning, so we made a strategic decision to hang out and wait for her to return.  In the several hours we stayed in the area, we did not see or hear the cubs at all until we saw their mother return. The family blended so well into the tall grass that we would have missed them completely if not for the experience of our guides. Taken on safari in South Africa. #bigcats

@jaydickmanphoto Southern rockhopper penguins march in from surf on Saunders Island in the Falkland Islands (Isla Malvinas.) The principal islands in the Falkland group are about 300 miles east of South America's Patagonian coast. Saunders is the 4th largest of the Falklands with an area of about 51 sq mi(132 km2)  Saunders has been identified as an Important Bird Area (IBA) by Birdlife International, with Falkland steamer ducks, ruddy-headed geese and several different type penguins.  This image shot with Olympus E-M1 w/12-40mm Pro Lens. @thephotosociety @natgeocreative

This image is featured in my book "Face to Face: Portraits of the Human Spirit." For more information visit http://www.alisonwright.com.

Photograph by @JohnStanmeyer

Balinese Hindus go into deep trance while looking out upon the water on the mystical and spiritual beach known as Petitenget Beach in Bali, Indonesia, as millions of Balinese celebrate Melasti, the sacred day of cleansing days before the start of Nyepi.

For more than five years, I have the privilege to live on the mystical island of Bali in Indonesia. Working on a story for National Geographic magazine, I delved deep into the mystical layers of how volcanoes — considered spiritual by many throughout the archipelago — are an important aspect in the lives of Indonesians.

Melasti is a very spiritual event, where tens of thousands of Balinese go to the ocean across the entire island, cleanings themselves before the run up to the day of silence or Nyepi — Nyepi just happened five days ago or on March 9.

Those with deep spiritual feelings often go into trance, taking sharp kris’s or daggers, trying to piece themselves. It is believed that spirits reside in the waters around Bali and in the mountains, which are volcanoes, protecting those in this very beautiful trance state.

Having witnessed countless Melasti's over the years, I have never once seen anyone pierce their skin, always protected by the spirits.

To see more about the unique culture of Bali, you can purchase my book, Island of the Spirits, through Amazon — go to my #Instagram page where there is a direct link to the book.

All my best,

John Stanmeyer

Photograph by @JohnStanmeyer

Farmers pond, silently veiled in trees, at a village on the outskirts of #Gyumri, #Armenia.

The other day was a time of deep wandering. While hosting a photo workshop in the ancient city of Gyumri, I needed space. Needed to breath. Meandering with my workshop co-instructor, photographer Anush Babajanyan and — follow @AnushBabajanyan here on IG for more beautiful, visual poems, of Armenia, the Caucasus and beyond —  we revisited a farm where one year ago Anush and I spent time at while working on a story for @NatGeo. This land of rolling fields offers so much to the eye, the heart, deeply welcoming, profoundly giving.

All my best, John Stanmeyer

Photo @chrisburkard // The wide open landscapes of Montana really bring you back to when times were simpler. Bison graze plains alongside winding back country roads and life seems to slow down. There’s a reason it’s nicknamed “big sky country” as skyscrapers are replaced by a seemingly never-ending expanse of blue, snow-capped mountains, on the distant horizon. If you’re looking to escape the hustle and bustle of city-life, this is the place.
